  "evidence": "All subscripts are modulo N, and all unrestricted index sums run from 0 to N−1. Put θ=2π/N, c=cos θ, λ=2−2c=4sin²(π/N), and Q(u)=E(u)−λM(u).\n\nCORRELATIONS AND REFLECTION AVERAGING. Direct expansion gives E(x)=2(R₀−R₁) and ∑ₘRₘ=(∑ⱼxⱼ)²=0. To supply the missing positivity certificate, define yⱼ^(r)=xⱼ−x_{r−j}. Then y_{r−j}^(r)=−yⱼ^(r). Writing dⱼ=x_{j+1}−xⱼ gives y_{j+1}^(r)−yⱼ^(r)=dⱼ+d_{r−j−1}. Since ∑dⱼ=0 and ∑xⱼ=0, expansion yields ∑ᵣE(y^(r))=2NE(x) and ∑ᵣM(y^(r))=2NM(x). Consequently ∑ᵣQ(y^(r))=2NQ(x).\n\nELEMENTARY FACTORIZATION. Fix r and abbreviate y=y^(r). Set sⱼ=sin(θ(j−r/2)). This sequence is periodic, satisfies s_{r−j}=−sⱼ, and obeys s_{j−1}+s_{j+1}=2csⱼ. Whenever sⱼ=0, we have 2j≡r modulo N, so yⱼ=0. Define tⱼ=yⱼ/sⱼ when sⱼ≠0 and tⱼ=0 otherwise. Thus yⱼ=sⱼtⱼ everywhere. Expanding the following finite sum and applying the sine recurrence proves the exact identity\nQ(y)=2c∑ⱼyⱼ²−2∑ⱼyⱼy_{j+1}=∑ⱼsⱼs_{j+1}(t_{j+1}−tⱼ)².\nIndeed, the coefficient of tⱼ² on the right is sⱼ(s_{j−1}+s_{j+1})=2csⱼ², including at zero entries.\n\nSIGN AUDIT. The sine zeros, as positions along the cyclic index line, are (r+kN)/2. Since θ<π, a negative product sⱼs_{j+1} entails exactly one intervening zero. Such a zero must be the half-integer j+1/2. Therefore r−j≡j+1 modulo N, giving y_{j+1}=−yⱼ, s_{j+1}=−sⱼ, and t_{j+1}=tⱼ. Every negatively weighted square therefore vanishes; zero weights contribute nothing. This proves Q(y)≥0 and supplies the explicit certificate\nQ(x)=(1/(2N))∑ᵣ ∑_{j: sⱼ^(r)s_{j+1}^(r)>0} sⱼ^(r)s_{j+1}^(r)(t_{j+1}^(r)−tⱼ^(r))²≥0.\nAll cyclic edges, including j=N−1, are included.\n\nCOMPLETE EQUALITY CHARACTERIZATION. For each r, the positive entries of s form one nonempty connected cyclic arc. Equality in Q(y) forces t constant on that arc, including when it is a singleton. Reflection gives the same constant on the negative arc; at zero entries y already vanishes. Hence Q(y^(r))=0 exactly when y^(r)=bᵣs^(r). If Q(x)=0, every nonnegative Q(y^(r)) vanishes. Since ∑ᵣyⱼ^(r)=Nxⱼ, we obtain xⱼ=N⁻¹∑ᵣbᵣsin(θ(j−r/2)), which is A cos(θj)+B sin(θj). Thus no additional equality cases occur.\n\nEXACT SHARPNESS CALCULATIONS. For z=exp(iθ), the finite geometric-sum formula gives ∑ⱼzʲ=∑ⱼz²ʲ=0 because z,z²≠1 for N≥3. Taking real and imaginary parts yields zero means for cosine and sine, ∑cos²(θj)=∑sin²(θj)=N/2, and ∑cos(θj)sin(θj)=0. The same squared and mixed identities hold with any common phase shift. For fⱼ=A cos(θj)+B sin(θj),\nf_{j+1}−fⱼ=2sin(θ/2)[−A sin(θ(j+1/2))+B cos(θ(j+1/2))].\nTherefore M(f)=N(A²+B²)/2 and E(f)=2Nsin²(π/N)(A²+B²). In particular, each individual cosine or sine has M=N/2 and E=2Nsin²(π/N); every real combination attains equality.\n\nBOUNDARY AUDIT. For N=3, zero mean gives x₀x₁+x₁x₂+x₂x₀=−M/2, so E=2M−2(x₀x₁+x₁x₂+x₂x₀)=3M, matching λ=3. For N=4, λ=2 and zero mean gives E−2M=−2(x₀+x₂)(x₁+x₃)=2(x₀+x₂)². Equality is exactly (A,B,−A,−B). The vector (1,−1,1,−1) has M=4 and E=16>2M=8.\n\nMETHODOLOGICAL CLASSIFICATION. This is an independent finite-sum positivity proof: the certificate is verified by expansion, sine addition, and reflection symmetry.
